items.headline: Skubal doesn't 'sympathize' with Dodgers critics
items.detail: New Dodgers pitcher Tarik Skubal said Monday he doesn't "really sympathize with people that blame the Dodgers for anything they've done," noting, "Every team could trade for me."

items.detail: The Red Sox acquired three-time All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman in a trade with the Baltimore Orioles, the biggest in a slew of deadline moves for Boston.

items.headline: Source: Yanks to call up top prospect Lombard
items.detail: The Yankees plan on calling up top prospect George Lombard Jr. on Tuesday after optioning shortstop Anthony Volpe to Triple-A, a source said.

items.headline: GM Cashman not ruling out anything with Judge
items.detail: Yankees GM Brian Cashman said Aaron Judge's status ultimately hinges on what the next imaging of the rib shows. He declined to share when he expects Judge to undergo that scan.

items.detail: The Guardians completed a trade with the Nationals to acquire left-hander Foster Griffin, and also made trades for outfielder Jo Adell and first baseman Nathaniel Lowe.

items.headline: Sources: Cristobal secures extension with Miami
items.detail: Miami coach Mario Cristobal, who led the Hurricanes to the College Football Playoff title game last season before losing to Indiana, agreed to a long-term contract extension with the school, sources told ESPN on Monday night, confirming a report.

items.headline: Sources: Knicks executive Rosas leaving team
items.detail: Knicks senior vice president of basketball operations Gersson Rosas is leaving the organization after four seasons, league sources confirmed to ESPN.

items.headline: Holmgren: OKC's departures were like losing family
items.detail: Oklahoma City's Chet Holmgren told reporters Saturday afternoon that the departures of three contributors to the Thunder's 2025 championship team felt "like losing a family member," but at the same time, "that's how the business of this game goes."
